title: Normalized separator payoff bound
statement: Let $X,Y\subseteq\mathbb{R}$, let $f:\mathbb{R}\times\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$, and let $u\subseteq Y$ be finite. Suppose $L:\mathbb{R}^{u}\to\mathbb{R}$ is a continuous linear functional such that $L(z)<L(c\mathbf{1})$ for every vector $z$ that strictly exceeds the payoff vector of some $x\in X$ in every coordinate of $u$. Let $W=\sum_{y\in u}-L(e_y)>0$, where $e_y$ is the coordinate unit vector. Then for every $x\in X$, $c\le\sum_{y\in u}\frac{-L(e_y)}{W}f(x,y)$.
hypotheses_covered: $L(z)<L(c\mathbf{1})$ for every vector in the finite upper image
replaced:
Let $X, Y \subseteq \bbr$, let $f : \bbr \to \bbr \to \bbr$ be a payoff, let $u$ be a
finite sample of columns from $Y$, and let $c \in \bbr$. Suppose $L : \bbr^u \to \bbr$
is a continuous linear functional separating the constant vector $(c,\dots,c)$ from the
finite upper image, i.e.\ $L(z) < L(c,\dots,c)$ for every $z \in U(X,f,u)$, and that
the total weight $W = \sum_{y \in u} \bigl(-L(e_y)\bigr)$ is strictly positive, where
$e_y$ is the standard basis vector at $y$. Then for every row $x \in X$,
\[
  c \;\le\; \sum_{y \in u} \frac{-L(e_y)}{W}\, f(x,y),
\]
that is, $c$ is at most the payoff of $x$ averaged under the normalized weights
$-L(e_y)/W$.
